rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: UKHSA guidance supports public-health management of hepatitis A cases and pre-exposure immunisation decisions.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Hepatitis A is an infectious liver disease spread through contamination from an infected person's faeces.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: The virus can remain on hands, food and surfaces and spread readily between people.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Vaccination and good hygiene are the principal preventive measures.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Public-health management includes assessment of contacts and targeted immunisation.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Symptoms can include fever, gastrointestinal illness and jaundice, although severity varies.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Management decisions should consider exposure setting, timing, vaccination history and vulnerability.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Most people recover, but serious liver disease can occur rarely.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Hepatitis A risk depends on exposure route, sanitation, food, travel, contact setting, immunity, timing and host factors.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: UKHSA hepatitis A evidence is case-, contact-, exposure-, vaccination-, setting- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: OPSS blind-cord child safety
rows.verified: Looped blind cords and chains can pose a strangulation danger to young children.

rows.source: OPSS blind-cord child safety
rows.verified: New looped-cord blinds must include child-safety devices at manufacture or sale.

rows.source: OPSS blind-cord child safety
rows.verified: Tidies and tensioners should be firmly fixed so the cord or chain remains held tight.

rows.source: OPSS blind-cord child safety
rows.verified: Older blinds may lack modern safety features and should be checked and made safer.

rows.source: OPSS blind-cord child safety
rows.verified: Cleats should be placed out of children's reach and spare cord secured after use.

rows.source: OPSS blind-cord child safety
rows.verified: OPSS campaigns emphasise removing accessible loops and keeping furniture away from blind cords.

rows.source: OPSS blind-cord child safety
rows.verified: Safety devices need correct installation and continued use to remain effective.

rows.source: OPSS blind-cord child safety
rows.verified: Blind-cord controls are intended to protect children and young visitors in homes.

rows.source: OPSS blind-cord child safety
rows.verified: Blind-cord risk depends on loop geometry, cord accessibility, installation, furniture position, child age, supervision and device condition.

rows.source: OPSS blind-cord child safety
rows.verified: OPSS blind-cord evidence is product-, installation-, room-, child-, use- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
